findings.title: queued default evaluated once at import time
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py the field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. The call to timezone.now() runs once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value shares the same timestamp. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence: provenance timestamps are wrong and any future debounce / ordering logic based on queued will be broken.

findings.title: to_dict/from_dict datetime does not survive task queue round-trip
findings.body: AssignmentSource.to_dict() in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py uses dataclasses.asdict, which leaves `queued` as a datetime object. src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py puts that dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` kwargs, which must be JSON serializable for Celery. After JSON round-trip the value comes back as a string, and AssignmentSource.from_dict() does `cls(**input_dict)` with no parsing, so `queued` becomes a str violating the declared datetime type. Consequence: task enqueue can fail or produce type-confused objects; serialization should use isoformat and parse back.

findings.title: Same-integration check does not stop multi-integration ping-pong
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py should_sync() returns False only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py fans outbound assignee sync out to every GroupLink for the group. If one Sentry group is linked to two different integrations A and B, an inbound assign from A is blocked from echoing to A but still syncs to B, B's webhook then re-enters as inbound from B and syncs to A, forming an infinite A->B->A loop. Consequence: the described fix only breaks single-integration echo, not the general issue-sync cycle.

findings.title: Missing coverage for allow-other-integration and deassign blocking
findings.body: In tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py the only cycle test is test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration which asserts outbound is suppressed when source equals target. There is no test that a different source integration still syncs outward, nor that deassign with a matching AssignmentSource is suppressed. Consequence: a regression that over-suppresses all outbound sync or that leaves the deassign loop unfixed would not be caught.
